relations.subject: search:sort-object
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate hasDefaultValue, corroborating the same default already recorded on search/search-request-params.json and on this batch's fts-scoring.json.
relations.evidence: FTS sorting is sorted by descending order of relevance. It can , however, be customized to sort by different fields, depending on the application.

relations.subject: search:sort-object
relations.object: last (missing values sort after other results)
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate hasDefaultValue, a second, distinct default value on the same sort-object concept (the `missing` sub-field).
relations.evidence: The value of `missing` can be `first`, in which case results with missing values appear _before_ other results; or `last` (the default), in which case they appear _after_.

relations.subject: search:sort-object
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate hasDefaultValue, a third distinct default on the same concept (the `mode` sub-field for multi-valued index fields).
relations.evidence: The `default` order is undefined but deterministic, allowing the paging of results from `from (_offset_)`, with reliable ordering.

relations.subject: search:sort-object
relations.evidence: Any document-field may be specified to hold the value on which sorting is to be based, provided that the field has been indexed in some way, whether dynamically or specifically.

notable_absence.finding: The page's own 'Sorting with Numeric' section promises a distinct numeric sort-value type ('You can specify the value of the `sort` field as a numeric type') but its example is identical in shape to the preceding object-sort example (an object with `by`/`field`/`mode`/`missing`/`type: number`) - there is no actual bare-numeric example anywhere on the page, so the section's own claim that `sort` accepts 'strings, objects, or numeric' as three distinct value shapes is not demonstrated for the third shape. Recorded as a gap between what the page claims and what it shows, not silently corrected.

cross_component_finding: No cross-component finding on this page - the `sort` mechanism it describes stays entirely inside the Search service's query response ordering.
